rootCauseAnalysis.summary: The data-processor sidecar continuously writes 1 MiB files every 5 seconds to a memory-backed emptyDir, causing unbounded memory-backed volume growth toward exhaustion. Deployment/data-service owns the pod-template configuration.
causalChain: Signal: `ContainerMemoryExhaustionPredicted` identifies `data-processor` in pod `data-service-6464fb6799-pczq5` as projected to exceed its memory limit.
Why? The sidecar has a 192Mi memory limit and continuously accumulates data in `/data`; the current pod usage is already 10Mi and growth is ongoing.
Why? The command writes one 1MiB file every 5 seconds, approximately 12MiB/minute, without cleanup.
Why? `/data` is backed by `emptyDir.medium: Memory` with a 256Mi size limit, so generated files consume memory-backed storage and can exhaust the finite volume in about 21–22 minutes.
Root cause: Deployment `data-service` contains an intentionally unbounded `data-processor` file-generation loop mounted onto a memory-backed, finite `emptyDir`; its pod template must be changed.

dueDiligence.targetAccuracy: Re-evaluated and confirmed `Deployment/data-service` is the correct target, not a node or derived Pod/ReplicaSet. The signal is generated from a child container, but the remediation must change the Deployment pod template that defines the sidecar command, its resources, and the memory-backed volume. The ReplicaSet and Pods are generated artifacts and are not durable remediation targets.
dueDiligence.proportionality: The issue affects both replicas but has one common, specific configuration source: the Deployment template. Modifying the Deployment is more precise and durable than changing individual Pods or the node. Node-wide remediation would be disproportionate because current node usage is low and no node-pressure evidence exists.
dueDiligence.scopeCompleteness: Checked the named Deployment, owning ReplicaSet, both replicas/pods, all relevant container configurations, current resource usage, namespace events, application and sidecar logs including previous-log attempts, node usage, and remediation context. No downstream Service or external dependency was named in the signal, and no evidence indicates they contribute. Previous-log calls correctly found no terminated containers.
dueDiligence.causalCompleteness: The chain was traced from the prediction to the exact container command, volume medium, volume limit, and Deployment-owned pod template. No deeper application source cause is available; the sidecar command itself is the deepest verified cause.
dueDiligence.evidenceSufficiency: Deployment and ReplicaSet manifests provide exact command, images, limits, requests, volume type, and size. Pod listing/top provides both affected pod names, readiness, zero restarts, and current usage. Events show successful scheduling/startup without OOM or eviction. App logs show normal startup. Prometheus discovery timed out, and node stats summary was forbidden on `nodes/proxy`; node top was available. The exact growth projection is calculated from the verified 1Mi/5-second loop, not from Prometheus.
dueDiligence.regressionAwareness: Remediation context reports no prior Tier 1 or Tier 2 remediation history and `regression_detected: false`; there is no failed remediation to work around.
dueDiligence.alternativeHypotheses: Node-wide memory pressure was considered and contradicted by node top showing 17% memory utilization and no pressure events. Existing OOM/restart was considered and contradicted by both pods having zero restarts and current Running/Ready status. Application-container failure was considered; its log only shows normal startup. Prometheus confirmation could not be obtained due to timeout, so a transient metric-specific alternative cannot be completely eliminated.
dueDiligence.confidenceCalibration: 0.93. Starting from 1.0, reduced by 0.04 because Prometheus metrics were inaccessible due to a request timeout, and by 0.03 because node stats summary was forbidden. The remaining evidence directly verifies the unbounded writer, memory-backed volume, limits, both affected replicas, and absence of current restarts/pressure.

contributingFactors: The data-processor writes approximately 12 MiB per minute indefinitely and never deletes files.
The /data emptyDir uses medium: Memory with a 256Mi size limit, while the sidecar has a 192Mi memory limit.
The Deployment has two replicas, so the behavior occurs in both pods.

kaResponse.analysis: The data-processor sidecar continuously writes 1 MiB files every 5 seconds to a memory-backed emptyDir, causing unbounded memory-backed volume growth toward exhaustion. Deployment/data-service owns the pod-template configuration.

rootCauseAnalysis.summary: The data-processor sidecar continuously writes 1 MiB files every 5 seconds to a memory-backed emptyDir, causing unbounded memory-backed volume growth toward exhaustion. Deployment/data-service owns the pod-template configuration.
causalChain: Signal: `ContainerMemoryExhaustionPredicted` identifies `data-processor` in pod `data-service-6464fb6799-pczq5` as projected to exceed its memory limit.
Why? The sidecar has a 192Mi memory limit and continuously accumulates data in `/data`; the current pod usage is already 10Mi and growth is ongoing.
Why? The command writes one 1MiB file every 5 seconds, approximately 12MiB/minute, without cleanup.
Why? `/data` is backed by `emptyDir.medium: Memory` with a 256Mi size limit, so generated files consume memory-backed storage and can exhaust the finite volume in about 21–22 minutes.
Root cause: Deployment `data-service` contains an intentionally unbounded `data-processor` file-generation loop mounted onto a memory-backed, finite `emptyDir`; its pod template must be changed.

dueDiligence.targetAccuracy: Re-evaluated and confirmed `Deployment/data-service` is the correct target, not a node or derived Pod/ReplicaSet. The signal is generated from a child container, but the remediation must change the Deployment pod template that defines the sidecar command, its resources, and the memory-backed volume. The ReplicaSet and Pods are generated artifacts and are not durable remediation targets.
dueDiligence.proportionality: The issue affects both replicas but has one common, specific configuration source: the Deployment template. Modifying the Deployment is more precise and durable than changing individual Pods or the node. Node-wide remediation would be disproportionate because current node usage is low and no node-pressure evidence exists.
dueDiligence.scopeCompleteness: Checked the named Deployment, owning ReplicaSet, both replicas/pods, all relevant container configurations, current resource usage, namespace events, application and sidecar logs including previous-log attempts, node usage, and remediation context. No downstream Service or external dependency was named in the signal, and no evidence indicates they contribute. Previous-log calls correctly found no terminated containers.
dueDiligence.causalCompleteness: The chain was traced from the prediction to the exact container command, volume medium, volume limit, and Deployment-owned pod template. No deeper application source cause is available; the sidecar command itself is the deepest verified cause.
dueDiligence.evidenceSufficiency: Deployment and ReplicaSet manifests provide exact command, images, limits, requests, volume type, and size. Pod listing/top provides both affected pod names, readiness, zero restarts, and current usage. Events show successful scheduling/startup without OOM or eviction. App logs show normal startup. Prometheus discovery timed out, and node stats summary was forbidden on `nodes/proxy`; node top was available. The exact growth projection is calculated from the verified 1Mi/5-second loop, not from Prometheus.
dueDiligence.regressionAwareness: Remediation context reports no prior Tier 1 or Tier 2 remediation history and `regression_detected: false`; there is no failed remediation to work around.
dueDiligence.alternativeHypotheses: Node-wide memory pressure was considered and contradicted by node top showing 17% memory utilization and no pressure events. Existing OOM/restart was considered and contradicted by both pods having zero restarts and current Running/Ready status. Application-container failure was considered; its log only shows normal startup. Prometheus confirmation could not be obtained due to timeout, so a transient metric-specific alternative cannot be completely eliminated.
dueDiligence.confidenceCalibration: 0.93. Starting from 1.0, reduced by 0.04 because Prometheus metrics were inaccessible due to a request timeout, and by 0.03 because node stats summary was forbidden. The remaining evidence directly verifies the unbounded writer, memory-backed volume, limits, both affected replicas, and absence of current restarts/pressure.

contributingFactors: The data-processor writes approximately 12 MiB per minute indefinitely and never deletes files.
The /data emptyDir uses medium: Memory with a 256Mi size limit, while the sidecar has a 192Mi memory limit.
The Deployment has two replicas, so the behavior occurs in both pods.
